pages.title: A11 · Data quality checks
lede: Objective (S3): apply data quality checks and validation rules to ensure reliable Silver and Gold datasets.
bronze.orders_nov4: 5006 ok, 5007 null customer_id, 5008 amount -15.00, 5009 unknown customer 105, 5010 ok. Only 5006 and 5010 may reach silver.orders.

blocks.heading: 1. Quality checklist and the action
blocks.code:
Not-null     customer_id IS NOT NULL         required keys present
Range        amount >= 0, no future dates    values possible
Referential  left join, then check the match every key exists
Action       warn | drop | quarantine | fail  decide before you code
blocks.note: Warn: soft problem, keep and count. Drop: useless row, no review. Quarantine: someone must fix it. Fail: the batch cannot be trusted.

blocks.heading: 2. Pipeline expectations (expected, from the docs)
blocks.code:
warn (default)  EXPECT (amount >= 0)                   dp.expect          5 rows written
drop            EXPECT (...) ON VIOLATION DROP ROW     dp.expect_or_drop  3 rows (5006 5009 5010)
fail            EXPECT (...) ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE  dp.expect_or_fail  0 rows, rolled back
blocks.note: 5009 slips through drop: no referential rule. No subquery on another table in a constraint. Metrics for warn and drop, none for fail.

blocks.heading: 3. Filter-or-quarantine snippet (observed, local Spark run)
blocks.code:
checked = (orders.join(customers_with_known_flag, "customer_id", "left")
  .withColumn("dq_reason",
    F.when(F.col("customer_id").isNull(), "null customer_id")
     .when(F.col("amount").isNull() | (F.col("amount") < 0), "bad amount")
     .when(F.col("known_customer").isNull(), "unknown customer"))
  .drop("known_customer"))
clean = checked.filter(F.col("dq_reason").isNull()).drop("dq_reason")
quarantine = checked.filter(F.col("dq_reason").isNotNull())
assert orders.count() == clean.count() + quarantine.count()   # 5 = 2 + 3
blocks.note: clean 5006, 5010 -> silver.orders (7 rows). quarantine 5007, 5008, 5009 with reason -> silver.orders_quarantine (3 rows).

pages.title: Constraints, traps, practice

blocks.heading: 4. Delta table constraints (observed, local Delta 4.0)
blocks.note: A CHECK behaves like fail, not drop. Primary key and foreign key constraints are informational only, not enforced.

blocks.heading: 5. The traps
blocks.text: 1) A warn-only check (no ON VIOLATION) while bad rows still reach gold. 2) Failing the whole load over a problem that affects one row. Also: a NULL amount passes neither filter("amount >= 0") nor filter("NOT (amount >= 0)") (observed 0 and 0), so check isNull() first. Free Edition: expectations run in Lakeflow pipelines (serverless pipelines use the Advanced edition, which includes expectations); one active pipeline per pipeline type.

blocks.heading: 6. Memory trick
blocks.text: Warn writes. Drop drops. Fail stops.

blocks.heading: Exam-style question
blocks.text: EXPECT (customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM silver.customers)) fails because a constraint cannot reference another table. Fix: left join orders to customers, select c.customer_id AS matched_customer_id, then EXPECT (matched_customer_id IS NOT NULL). Foreign keys are not enforced; Python has the same rule.

blocks.heading: Practice challenge
blocks.text: Q1 DROP ROW pipeline: which bad order still reaches silver? 5009 (customer 105), no referential rule (expected: 5006, 5009, 5010). Q2 CHECK (amount >= 0), one INSERT of 5008 (-15.00) + 5012 (9.00): neither row, the whole insert fails (observed: still 7 rows). Q3 NULL amount 5011 split with filter("amount >= 0") / filter("NOT (amount >= 0)"): neither side (observed 0 and 0); the snippet quarantines it as bad amount.
